forbidden_standalone_uses: F1 alone for imbalanced prediction tasks (masks recall/precision tradeoff at imbalance, e.g. failure prediction with <1% positive rate)
AUROC alone for any operational-readiness claim (an 'always fires' predictor can have nominally positive AUROC while being false-alarm-rate ~1.0 and operationally useless)
accuracy alone for abstention safety (an always-answer policy can have high accuracy while carrying unacceptable unsafe-action rate on the abstained-would-have-been-wrong cases)

executor self-report alone for recovery success (Recovery.executor_self_report is EXECUTOR_SELF_REPORT_UNVALIDATED by construction; only validation.validation_status, OBSERVED_OUTCOME_VALIDATED, is eligible)

metrics.name: Area Under ROC Curve
metrics.mathematical_definition: P(score(positive) > score(negative)) over all positive/negative pairs, i.e. the Mann-Whitney U statistic normalized to [0,1].
metrics.interpretation: Ranking quality: how often a random positive is scored above a random negative.
metrics.failure_mode: High AUROC with false-alarm-rate ~1.0 at any usable threshold means ranking is fine but no usable operating point exists (see PRED-OOM).
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Requires >=10 of the minority class for a bootstrap CI to be meaningful; report Wilson/bootstrap CI always, never a bare point estimate.
known_pathological_cases: single-class family (undefined AUROC)
always-fires predictor with high AUROC but false-alarm-rate 1.0
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Never sufficient alone for an operational-readiness claim; must be paired with MET-FALSE-ALARM-RATE.

metrics.name: Area Under Precision-Recall Curve
metrics.mathematical_definition: Integral of precision(recall) over recall in [0,1].
metrics.interpretation: Ranking quality under class imbalance, more sensitive to positive-class performance than AUROC.
metrics.failure_mode: Baseline AUPRC equals the positive base rate, not 0 — must always be compared against that base rate, never against 0.5.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Same as AUROC; especially unstable under <10 positives.
known_pathological_cases: reporting AUPRC without stating the positive base rate makes the number uninterpretable

metrics.name: Brier Score
metrics.mathematical_definition: mean((predicted_probability - outcome)^2) over all instances.
metrics.interpretation: Joint calibration+discrimination score; decomposes into reliability, resolution, uncertainty.
metrics.failure_mode: A constant predictor at the base rate can achieve a deceptively low Brier score under strong imbalance.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Stable at moderate n (>100); report alongside ECE and AUROC to disambiguate calibration from discrimination contributions.
known_pathological_cases: low Brier from a trivial constant predictor under imbalance

metrics.name: Expected Calibration Error
metrics.mathematical_definition: sum_b (n_b/N) * |acc(b) - conf(b)| over B confidence bins b.
metrics.interpretation: How far predicted confidence deviates from empirical accuracy, bin-averaged.
metrics.failure_mode: ECE can improve (via temperature scaling) while AUROC stays flat — this is the sentiment finding and MUST be reported as a distinct fact, never presented as 'uncertainty improved' in aggregate.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Bin count must be chosen relative to n; too many bins with small n produces unstable per-bin estimates.
known_pathological_cases: ECE improvement mistaken for AUROC improvement
bin-count-dependent instability
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Must never be the sole metric used to claim a discrimination improvement.

metrics.name: Risk-Coverage Curve
metrics.mathematical_definition: risk(c) = error rate among the top-c-fraction most-confident predictions, for c in [0,1].
metrics.unit: curve; scalar summary = area under the curve (AURC)
metrics.interpretation: How error rate trades off against the fraction of instances the system is willing to answer.
metrics.failure_mode: A flat risk-coverage curve near the base error rate indicates the confidence signal carries little selective value.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Needs enough samples per coverage bucket (>=20) to avoid noisy risk estimates at low coverage.
known_pathological_cases: degenerate curve when confidence ties are frequent (arithmetic agreement_rate has few distinct values)

metrics.name: Selective Risk
metrics.mathematical_definition: error rate among instances where the policy chooses to ANSWER (excludes ABSTAIN/REVIEW instances).
metrics.interpretation: Error rate conditional on the system actually acting.
metrics.failure_mode: Can be driven to 0 by an always-abstain policy with coverage->0; must always be reported jointly with MET-COVERAGE.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Requires nonzero coverage; undefined at coverage=0 (must report as undefined, not 0).
known_pathological_cases: always-abstain 'wins' if coverage is not jointly reported
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Must always be reported with MET-COVERAGE.

metrics.name: Coverage
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of instances where decision.action != ABSTAIN.
metrics.interpretation: How often the system is willing to act.
metrics.failure_mode: Coverage alone says nothing about correctness.
known_pathological_cases: coverage=1.0 (always-answer) is not inherently good or bad without selective risk

metrics.name: Abstention Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: 1 - coverage.
metrics.interpretation: Fraction of instances abstained.
metrics.failure_mode: High abstention rate on genuinely easy/high-confidence cases indicates over-conservative policy (see MET-UNNECESSARY-ABSTENTION).
known_pathological_cases: abstention rate = 1.0 trivially maximizes safety metrics while destroying utility

metrics.name: Unnecessary Abstention Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of ABSTAIN decisions where the withheld answer would in fact have been correct (agent_output.is_correct == true had it answered).
metrics.interpretation: Cost of over-conservatism.
metrics.failure_mode: Trades off directly against unsafe-action rate; must be reported alongside it, not alone.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Requires >=20 ABSTAIN instances for a stable estimate.
known_pathological_cases: 0% requires coverage=1.0, which reintroduces unsafe-action risk elsewhere

metrics.name: Final Correctness Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of ANSWER/RETRY-resolved decisions where the final answer equals ground truth.
metrics.interpretation: End-user-visible correctness after the abstention policy is applied.
metrics.failure_mode: Can look artificially high if coverage is low (easy cases retained, hard cases abstained).
known_pathological_cases: cherry-picked high correctness at near-zero coverage

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.mathematical_definition: TP / (TP + FP)
metrics.interpretation: Of all raised alarms, fraction that were real failures.
metrics.failure_mode: Meaningless without recall context (trivial precision=1.0 by never firing).
known_pathological_cases: precision=1.0 via near-zero recall

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.mathematical_definition: TP / (TP + FN)
metrics.interpretation: Of all real failures, fraction detected.
metrics.failure_mode: Trivially 1.0 for an always-fires predictor.
known_pathological_cases: recall=1.0 via always-fires, meaningless without false-alarm-rate
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Never sufficient alone; must be paired with MET-FALSE-ALARM-RATE.

metrics.name: False Alarm Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: FP / (FP + TN)
metrics.interpretation: Of all non-failures, fraction incorrectly flagged. This is the project's own deciding operational-validity metric.
metrics.failure_mode: An 'always fires' predictor has false-alarm-rate ~1.0 regardless of a nominally positive AUROC; per the project's own P3-W5 discipline this DISQUALIFIES the family from STRONG_EVIDENCE/PLAUSIBLE grading regardless of AUROC.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Requires a meaningful negative-class sample; unstable under extreme imbalance.
known_pathological_cases: false-alarm-rate 1.00 while AUROC nominally >0.7 (the exact OOM/cpu/flaky pattern in this project)

metrics.name: Specificity
metrics.mathematical_definition: TN / (TN + FP) = 1 - false_alarm_rate
metrics.interpretation: True-negative rate.
metrics.failure_mode: Same as false-alarm-rate, inverted.
known_pathological_cases: specificity 0.179 on the OOM subset at its calibrated operating point, per the master record

metrics.name: Lead Time
metrics.mathematical_definition: failure_detected_time - prediction_time, for correctly predicted failures.
metrics.interpretation: How far in advance the prediction fires relative to the actual failure.
metrics.failure_mode: A trivial lead time near 0 provides no operational value even with high recall.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Report mean and distribution, not mean alone (skew is common).
known_pathological_cases: near-zero lead time technically 'correct' but operationally useless

metrics.name: Useful Lead Time Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of correctly-predicted failures with lead_time > 10ms (project's own minimum-useful threshold).
metrics.interpretation: Fraction of detections that arrive early enough to plausibly act on.
metrics.failure_mode: None beyond threshold arbitrariness, which must be disclosed as a fixed, documented choice (10ms), not silently varied per family to flatter results.
known_pathological_cases: threshold gaming by choosing a smaller cutoff post hoc

metrics.name: Failure-Class Accuracy
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of diagnosis.suspected_cause matching failure.failure_class, computed ONLY where failure.failure_class exists as ground truth.
metrics.interpretation: Nearest available diagnosis-quality proxy; explicitly NOT identical to 'correct diagnosis' (a failure_class match is necessary, not sufficient, for a genuinely correct root-cause diagnosis).
metrics.failure_mode: Overstating this as full diagnosis correctness rather than a proxy.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Requires >=30 per failure class; most classes in the current dataset are below this.
known_pathological_cases: 100% match rate does not promote suspected_cause to ground truth status

metrics.name: Evidence Correctness
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of diagnosis evidence citations that are drawn from the current run_id only (per _eligible_current_incident boundary), never a later or cross-run event.
metrics.interpretation: Whether the diagnosis mechanism respects the cross-run-contamination boundary (EVALUATION_INCIDENT_001's fix).
metrics.failure_mode: A silent regression of this boundary would look like improved diagnosis accuracy while being a leakage violation.
known_pathological_cases: cross-run contamination masquerading as improved accuracy

metrics.name: Temporal Integrity
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of diagnosis/decision/prediction records whose DecisionTimeContract ordering (snapshot <= generated <= decision) holds.
metrics.interpretation: Mechanical leakage check, not a system-quality score per se.
metrics.failure_mode: Any violation must exclude the record from scoring, not merely penalize it.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: n/a (should be 100% or the record is a data-quality defect).
known_pathological_cases: treating a violation as 'mostly fine' instead of excluding the record

metrics.name: Contradiction Handling Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of cases with conflicting evidence where the diagnosis mechanism emits UNKNOWN or a hedged confidence rather than a confident single cause.
metrics.interpretation: Whether the system correctly recognizes irreducible ambiguity.
metrics.failure_mode: Confidently resolving a genuinely contradictory case is a worse failure than abstaining from diagnosis.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Requires identifying contradiction cases, which may be rare in the current dataset (LIMITED).
known_pathological_cases: overconfident resolution of contradictory evidence

metrics.name: UNKNOWN Handling Correctness
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of episodes where suspected_cause=null (UNKNOWN) is emitted exactly on episodes where causal_status=CAUSAL_GROUND_TRUTH_UNAVAILABLE, neither more nor less often.
metrics.interpretation: A system correctly saying UNKNOWN must not be penalized for not hallucinating a cause (design principle) — this metric rewards, not penalizes, correct UNKNOWN.
metrics.failure_mode: Scoring UNKNOWN as a wrong answer inverts the intended incentive and must never be done.
known_pathological_cases: treating UNKNOWN as an automatic miss

metrics.name: Unsupported-Cause Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of non-UNKNOWN diagnoses whose cited evidence does not actually support the stated cause under re-inspection.
metrics.interpretation: Measures fabrication/overreach in diagnosis output.
metrics.failure_mode: None beyond needing a re-inspection protocol, itself LIMITED where no independent evidence exists.
known_pathological_cases: plausible-sounding but unsupported causal narratives

metrics.name: False Causal Attribution Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of episodes where causal_status=CAUSAL_GROUND_TRUTH_UNAVAILABLE but the system nonetheless emits a confident, non-UNKNOWN causal claim, where measurable.
metrics.interpretation: Direct hallucination-of-cause rate.
metrics.failure_mode: Only measurable where causal ground truth's unavailability itself is independently knowable, which is LIMITED in the current dataset.
known_pathological_cases: measurement itself limited by lack of independent unavailability ground truth

metrics.name: Recovery Success Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of recovery_action attempts with validation.validation_status == RECOVERED (OBSERVED_OUTCOME_VALIDATED only).
metrics.interpretation: Independently-validated recovery effectiveness.
metrics.failure_mode: Substituting executor_self_report inflates this metric artificially; forbidden by leakage rule 8.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: Report per action-family (RECONFIGURE/RETRY/etc), never pooled, per design principle.
known_pathological_cases: 0% on a genuinely unfixable deterministic failure is VALID, not a bad result

metrics.name: Unsafe Action Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of recovery actions where safety.unsafe_authorization == true.
metrics.interpretation: Hard zero-tolerance gate metric; never traded off against recovery-rate.
metrics.failure_mode: Any nonzero rate here should independently fail the track, regardless of how high recovery-rate is.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: n/a; even n=1 unsafe action is reportable and disqualifying.
known_pathological_cases: masked by a high recovery-rate headline number if not reported jointly

metrics.name: Unnecessary Recovery Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of recovery actions initiated where failure.failure_detected was actually a false alarm (no real failure existed).
metrics.interpretation: Cost of acting on false predictions.
metrics.failure_mode: Directly downstream of MET-FALSE-ALARM-RATE; an always-fires predictor will always show high unnecessary-recovery-rate.
known_pathological_cases: masked if only recovery-success-rate on true-positive cases is reported

metrics.name: Action-Selection Accuracy
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of episodes where the selected recovery.action_type matches the action with the highest independently-known efficacy for that failure_class, where such efficacy ground truth exists (e.g. RECONFIGURE for contended-port).
metrics.interpretation: Whether the planner picks the empirically-best action when one is known.
metrics.failure_mode: Only computable where efficacy ground truth exists per failure_class/context; otherwise NOT_EVALUABLE for that slice.
known_pathological_cases: no defined 'best action' for some failure classes (e.g. GPU_DEVICE_FAILURE, NOT_APPLICABLE)

metrics.name: Time/Cost Overhead
metrics.mathematical_definition: wall-clock or resource cost of the recovery attempt relative to a no-recovery baseline.
metrics.interpretation: Practical cost of the recovery mechanism.
metrics.failure_mode: None beyond needing a consistent cost accounting method across families.
known_pathological_cases: comparing costs across incompatible environments without normalization

metrics.name: Validation Correctness
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of validation.validation_status determinations independently re-derivable from raw post-recovery telemetry (SignalRecoveryValidator's own re-derivation, not executor_self_report).
metrics.interpretation: Confidence in the validator itself, distinct from confidence in the recovery action.
metrics.failure_mode: If the validator itself is unreliable, all downstream recovery metrics inherit that unreliability.
known_pathological_cases: a validator that agrees with executor_self_report too often may itself be compromised

metrics.name: Memory Retrieval Precision
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of memory_interaction reads whose retrieved MemoryRecord's (workload_id, environment_id, failure_class) matches the querying episode's own scope.
metrics.interpretation: Whether retrieval respects the documented scoping contract, never merely semantic similarity.
metrics.failure_mode: Any cross-scope retrieval not explicitly allowed is a contamination event, not merely imprecise.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: n/a; even n=1 violation is reportable.
known_pathological_cases: cross-workload retrieval justified only by semantic similarity

metrics.name: Repeated-Incident Adaptation Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of repeated-workload_id sequences where the action taken on run N+1 differs from run N following an intervening memory write, AND the outcome improves.
metrics.interpretation: Direct measure of the memory ON vs OFF contrast (retry->retry->reconfigure->recovered pattern).
metrics.failure_mode: Requires genuinely repeated workload_id sequences to exist; NOT_EVALUABLE otherwise (current dataset gap, see MEM-EVAL).
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: n>=10 repeated sequences for any aggregate claim.
known_pathological_cases: decision changes without outcome improvement (churn, not adaptation)

metrics.name: Decision Change Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of repeated-workload_id pairs where decision.action differs before vs after a memory write, regardless of outcome.
metrics.interpretation: Measures 'memory influences decision' as distinct from 'memory improves outcome' (design principle: 4 separate claims).
metrics.failure_mode: Must never be reported as if it alone proved memory improves outcomes.
known_pathological_cases: high change rate with no outcome improvement (noise, not learning)
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Never sufficient alone to claim 'memory improves outcome' — must be paired with MET-RECOVERY-IMPROVEMENT.

metrics.name: Recovery Improvement (memory ON vs OFF)
metrics.mathematical_definition: recovery_success_rate(memory=ON) - recovery_success_rate(memory=OFF), matched on workload_id/environment_id/failure_class.
metrics.interpretation: The causal contribution of memory, isolated by the ON/OFF ablation.
metrics.failure_mode: Confounded if retry is also enabled differently between arms (must be disclosed as in the project's own predictor/retry confound).
known_pathological_cases: small-n confound with a co-varying causal factor (retry)

metrics.name: Cross-Workload Contamination Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of memory reads that retrieve a MemoryRecord scoped to a different workload_id than the querying episode's own.
metrics.interpretation: Hard leakage/contamination check.
metrics.failure_mode: Any nonzero rate (absent explicit design allowance) is a specification violation.
known_pathological_cases: silently allowed 'similar workload' retrieval

metrics.name: Cross-Environment Contamination Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of memory reads that retrieve a MemoryRecord scoped to a different environment_id than the querying episode's own.
metrics.interpretation: Same as above, environment axis.
metrics.failure_mode: Same as above.
known_pathological_cases: identical to cross-workload contamination pattern

metrics.name: Temporal Leakage Rate (memory)
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of memory reads whose retrieved MemoryRecord.recorded_at is after the querying episode's decision_time.
metrics.interpretation: Direct check of leakage rule 5/9.
metrics.failure_mode: Any nonzero rate invalidates every downstream memory-effect claim for the affected episodes.
known_pathological_cases: approximated timestamps masking a real violation

metrics.name: Persistence Correctness
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of memory records that survive a simulated restart and remain retrievable under the same scope contract.
metrics.interpretation: Whether memory is durable, not merely in-process.
metrics.failure_mode: Mechanical check; not sample-size sensitive.
known_pathological_cases: in-memory-only store silently losing records across a restart boundary

metrics.name: Ranking Generalization Degradation
metrics.mathematical_definition: AUROC(development) - AUROC(held_out or robustness), reported per environment transition, never as a single blended number.
metrics.interpretation: How much ranking quality degrades zero-shot across environments.
metrics.failure_mode: Collapsing dev/held-out/robustness into one number erases the actual degradation curve (OOM: 0.989->0.983->0.935).
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: n>=300 per environment for a stable AUROC estimate.
known_pathological_cases: reporting only the best environment's number
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Must always be reported per environment transition, never pooled into one score.

metrics.name: Operating-Point Generalization
metrics.mathematical_definition: false_alarm_rate/precision at the SAME dev-calibrated fixed threshold, applied zero-shot to held_out/robustness, compared to its dev-split value.
metrics.interpretation: Whether a fixed decision threshold, not just the ranking, transfers.
metrics.failure_mode: Must be reported as a metric DISTINCT from ranking generalization; the OOM finding is exactly 'ranking transfers, operating point does not' and collapsing them erases this.
metrics.direction: higher_is_better (closer to dev value is better)
known_pathological_cases: silently re-calibrating the threshold on held_out data, which would be a leakage violation, not a generalization result
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Must never be merged with MET-RANKING-GENERALIZATION-DEGRADATION into one number.

metrics.name: End-to-End Recovery Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of full-loop episodes reaching outcome_class=RECOVERED, independently validated.
metrics.interpretation: Headline full-loop success metric.
metrics.failure_mode: Can mask a disqualified predictor or unsafe recovery subsystem if reported alone (masking failure, see E2E-EVAL).
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: n>=30 for the current dataset's 46-record controlled_runtime scope; LIMITED below that.
known_pathological_cases: good recovery hiding an invalid predictor or unsafe action, per the design principle
metrics.forbidden_standalone_use: Must always be reported alongside every component-level metric (uncertainty, prediction, diagnosis, recovery, memory) for the same episodes.

metrics.name: End-to-End Unsafe-Action Rate
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of full-loop episodes with any safety.unsafe_authorization==true at any stage.
metrics.interpretation: Hard gate; zero-tolerance metric at the system level.
metrics.failure_mode: Any nonzero value should independently disqualify an end-to-end 'success' claim regardless of recovery rate.
known_pathological_cases: averaged away in an aggregate success score

metrics.name: Reproducibility / Test-Order Independence Indicator
metrics.mathematical_definition: fraction of repeated full-suite runs (same seeds, same code) producing byte-identical or statistically identical results, and independence from test execution order.
metrics.interpretation: System-health metric alongside the research metrics — a proxy for whether the evaluation harness itself is trustworthy.
metrics.failure_mode: Silent nondeterminism (unseeded randomness, dict/set iteration order, wall-clock dependence) would inflate or deflate other metrics unpredictably across runs.
metrics.minimum_sample_considerations: n/a; a single detected nondeterminism is a defect to fix, not average away.
known_pathological_cases: Python hash()-dependent ordering silently changing results run to run
